If many of them refer to one area's problem, for example the same free-tier change, that area's total is understated; the labels cannot show which area that would be.

Premium-only boundary, upper-bound sensitivity (computed by code; `analysis/premium_only_sensitivity.json`): 4785 (T56) of the 18016 (C01) `billing.premium_only` complaint and cancellation records contain no Premium or payment word (premium, subscri-, pay/paid/paying, free, buy, money, trial, $; case-insensitive), with a severity sum of 14239 (T57). If none of them belonged to billing/support, its severity sum would fall from 59146 (A02) to 44907 (T58), below usability 54124 (A05) and playback/performance 46058 (A08). This is an upper bound, not a relabelling: many of these reviews plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle), and they were not moved to any other area.
mandatory_limitations: Counts describe the labeled reviews in the declared analysis scope of 200,013 reviews (analysis_200k.csv, a deterministic uniform sample of the 660,622-review corpus plus every empty-text row): self-selected public app reviews, not a customer population. They carry no revenue, plan tier or confirmed cancellations, so revenue at risk cannot be computed.
Cancellation language is expressed intent, not observed churn; nothing here estimates a causal effect on retention.
Star ratings and helpful votes were not used to classify; severity is judged from the text under the shared rubric.
16964 completed records are flagged needs_review, 13 are quarantined and 0 are unfinished.
The analysis covers a uniform random sample of the corpus, not every review; shares carry sampling error (intervals shown) and the 460,609 out-of-scope reviews were ingested but not classified.

Golden set (evals/golden/results.json): on 50 human-labelled reviews the pipeline's labels match the human labels on topic 76%, intent 74% and severity 76% (exact); 50 cases are a diagnostic of label quality, not a precise accuracy estimate.

alternatives.why_not_first: Usability has severity sum {A05} across {A04} complaint and cancellation reviews, below billing/support's {A02}, even though it leads on share of complaints {T19} and complaint count {A04}; on the enricher's baseline metric it ranks second.

Playback/performance has severity sum {A08} across {A07} reviews, below billing/support's {A02}, and its share of reviews fell {T15} between {T01} and {T02} (from {T13} to {T14}), the only decline among the four decision areas, though the verifier's labelling ranks it first on severity sum ({T46}).

Access/onboarding has the lowest severity sum, {A17} across {A16} reviews, and the lowest share of complaints {T28} (interval {T29} to {T30}), despite a rise in share of reviews of {T09} between {T01} and {T02}.

limitations: The verifier's own severity-sum ordering on its {T41}-review sample puts playback/performance ahead of billing/support, so the recommendation is provisional pending a larger or reconciled verification sample.
The spike months {T31} and {T35} describe shares of reviews in those specific months only; whether the elevated premium-only share in {T35} (+{T38}) persists beyond the review window is not shown.

Golden-set and verifier agreement rates (topic, intent, severity) are below full agreement, so issue-to-area assignment, including the boundary between billing.premium_only and other areas, carries some uncertainty not captured in the severity-sum totals.

The period comparison between {T01} and {T02} uses self-selected reviews with different total volumes ({T03} versus {T05} reviews), so the share changes describe compositional shifts in who reviewed, not a measured change in the underlying customer base.
next_quarter_actions: Review the scope and communication of free-tier skip, shuffle, repeat and rewind restrictions tied to billing.premium_only, and test clearer in-app explanation or a narrower restriction; watch whether severity sum {C02} and complaint count {C01} move down next period.

Investigate the spike in {T35}, where billing.premium_only's share of reviews rose by {T38} versus other months, to see whether a specific rollout or change drove the jump, and check whether the later-period share of reviews for billing/support ({T11}, up {T12} from {T10}) continues to grow or levels off.

As a hedge, examine excessive ad interruptions (usability.ads, severity sum {C10} across {C09} complaint and cancellation reviews, mean severity {C11}) for quick frequency or placement adjustments, since usability leads on share of complaints {T19} and complaint count {A04}.
rationale: Billing/support's severity sum {A02} across {A01} complaint and cancellation reviews is the highest among the four decision areas, led by Premium-only restrictions with severity sum {C02} across {C01} reviews and mean severity {C03}.

Trend supports billing/support: among the four decision areas it shows the largest increase in share of reviews between {T01} and {T02}, rising {T12} (from {T10} to {T11}), while playback/performance fell {T15} and usability and access rose only {T18} and {T09} respectively.

Billing/support's share of complaints {T22} (interval {T23} to {T24}) does not overlap with usability's higher share {T19} (interval {T20} to {T21}) or playback/performance's {T25}; usability leads on share of complaints and complaint count {A04}, even though billing/support leads on severity sum.

Robustness caveat: the independent verifier, on its labelling of the same {T41} sampled reviews, ranks playback/performance first on severity sum ({T46} versus billing/support's {T48}), disagreeing with the enricher's ordering that puts billing/support first ({T42} versus playback/performance's {T44}); this is a labelling disagreement, not noise, and makes the call provisional.

The premium-only sensitivity check is an upper bound only: removing the {T56} premium-only records that contain no Premium or payment word (severity sum {T57}) would drop billing/support's severity sum to {T58}, below usability's {A05} and playback/performance's {A08}, though the interpretation notes the real effect is likely smaller.
output.recommendation: Billing/support carries the highest baseline priority among the four decision areas, with severity sum {A02} across {A01} complaint and cancellation reviews, almost entirely driven by the Premium-only restrictions issue (severity sum {C02} across {C01} complaint and cancellation reviews, mean severity {C03}). This issue is free-tier packaging and entitlement policy - what the free tier includes (skip limits, forced shuffle, inability to pick, repeat or rewind songs) and how changes are rolled out and explained - not a payment, charging or checkout defect, so the work belongs with pricing and monetization rather than a support-ticket backlog.
what_would_change_the_call: The verifier's severity ordering holding on a larger verified sample beyond {T41}, confirming playback/performance ({T46}) ahead of billing/support ({T48}) rather than the enricher's ordering ({T42} ahead of {T44}).

A human audit of the {T56} premium-only records without a payment word (severity sum {T57}) finding most are genuinely about free-tier restrictions would weaken this caveat; finding most are mislabeled would strengthen the case that billing/support's lead is overstated, since removal brings its severity sum to {T58}.
Billing/support's share of reviews reversing in the same months of the following year rather than continuing the rise from {T10} to {T11} seen between {T01} and {T02}.

payload.question: Where should the next quarter of product-improvement effort go: access/onboarding, usability, playback/performance, or billing/support?

top_issues.summary: Customers report that core playback features like song selection, skipping, repeat, and full-song playback are locked behind a Premium paywall.

top_issues.definition: General praise or criticism with no specific feature, unrelated content (politics, artists, boycotts), or meaningless text.
top_issues.name: General or unrelated

top_issues.definition: Too many, too long, too loud or repeated ads; ads interrupting listening.
top_issues.name: Excessive ad interruptions
top_issues.summary: Customers report that frequent, repeated ads interrupt music and podcast listening, causing irritation and frustration with the app.

top_issues.definition: Music stops, pauses, skips by itself, will not start, or plays the wrong song.
top_issues.name: Playback stops or skips unexpectedly
top_issues.summary: Customers report that playback randomly pauses, stops, fails to start, or plays the wrong track, disrupting their listening experience.

top_issues.definition: Managing the queue, playlists, liked songs or library; shuffle or repeat controls that misbehave.

top_issues.definition: Cannot log in, keeps getting logged out, login or verification-code errors.

period_comparison.comparison_scope: areas lists the four decision areas only; areas that are not decision options are under non_decision_areas
period_comparison.method: share = complaint/cancellation reviews in the area / all classified reviews in the period; Wilson 95% intervals; identical calendar months one year apart avoid the partial first/last months and seasonal mix. Descriptive only: reviews are self-selected, not a customer census.

premium_only_sensitivity.interpretation: Upper-bound sensitivity, not a relabelling. It assumes that none of the records without a Premium or payment word belongs in billing/support and adds them to no other area. Many of them plainly describe free-tier limits without naming Premium (skip limits, forced shuffle, no repeat or rewind), and non-English payment words (for example 'paisa') are not matched, so the real effect is smaller than shown.
premium_only_sensitivity.what: upper-bound sensitivity of the billing/support lead to the premium-only topic boundary, computed by code; not a relabelling
